# jsonstor-browser

> Home: [http://jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com)
>
> Version: 0.1.0

### The browser storages: local storage, the Origin Private File System, and IndexedDB.

Overview
---------------------------------------------------------------------

`jsonstor` defines one interface for working with a document store and implements it
  for a variety of database products and file formats. The interface is the same whichever
  adapter is underneath, so the storage a project uses becomes a configuration decision
  rather than a structural one.

This package is one such adapter. The browser storages: local storage, the Origin Private File System, and IndexedDB.

***It carries no database driver.*** The server is reached over HTTP with the runtime's
  own `fetch`, so this package adds nothing to a project beyond `jsonstor` and `jsongin`.

See [`@liquicode/jsonstor`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsonstor) for the interface,
  and [jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com) for the documentation.

Getting Started
---------------------------------------------------------------------

```bash
npm install --save @liquicode/jsonstor-browser
```

```js
const jsonstor = require( '@liquicode/jsonstor' )();
jsonstor.LoadPlugin( require( '@liquicode/jsonstor-browser' ) );

let storage = jsonstor.GetStorage( 'jsonstor-browser', {
	Key: '...',
	Path: '...',
	DatabaseName: '...',
	CollectionName: '...',
	AutoFlush: true,
	PrimaryKey: "_id",
	PrimaryKeyMutable: false,
	HostIndex: false,
} );
```

Versions
---------------------------------------------------------------------

This package answers to more than one name. Pass any of these to `GetStorage()`;
  a name which is not listed is refused.

| Name | Dialect it uses | Measured against |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| `jsonstor-browser-localstorage` | its own | - |
| `jsonstor-browser-opfs` | its own | - |
| `jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` | its own | - |

A name with its own dialect was measured against that server version and covers every
  later one up to the next such name. The rest resolve to one of those. The bare name
  follows the newest dialect this package carries, which is what most callers want.

A name whose dialect your server cannot serve is refused on the first operation, naming
  the version you asked for and the one the server needs.

Settings
---------------------------------------------------------------------

| Setting | Required | Default | Description |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `Key` | ***Yes*** | - | ***`jsonstor-browser-localstorage` only.*** The `localStorage` key this collection is stored under. One key holds one collection; name a second key for a second collection. |
| `Path` | ***Yes*** | - | ***`jsonstor-browser-opfs` only.*** The path within the Origin Private File System holding this collection. Folders along it are created as needed. |
| `DatabaseName` | ***Yes*** | - | ***`jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` only.*** The IndexedDB database holding this collection. It is created if it does not exist. |
| `CollectionName` | ***Yes*** | - | ***`jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` only.*** The object store this storage reads and writes. One database holds as many collections as you name. |
| `AutoFlush` | No | `true` | ***The two blob storages only.*** Write the collection out after every insert, update, replacement or delete. Turn it off to batch a run of writes and call `FlushStorage()` yourself. `jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` writes a record at a time and has nothing to flush. |
| `PrimaryKey` | No | `"_id"` | The field which holds the identifier. Set it to the key field of an existing store. |
| `PrimaryKeyMutable` | No | `false` | Allow an update or replacement to change the identifier. When `false`, such an operation is refused. |
| `HostIndex` | No | `false` | ***The two blob storages only.*** Hold an index over the identifier, so a lookup by it costs one entry rather than the whole collection. Off by default, because an index over a store something else writes goes stale - call `RefreshIndex()` when it might have. `jsonstor-browser-indexeddb` hosts its own index and takes no such setting. |

Peculiarities
---------------------------------------------------------------------

- ***These storages run only in a browser.*** Constructing one in Node is refused. Load the package from the browser bundle, with `jsonstor`.
- ***Choose one of three names***: `jsonstor-browser-localstorage`, `jsonstor-browser-opfs` or `jsonstor-browser-indexeddb`. The package name `jsonstor-browser` is refused.
- ***`jsonstor-browser-localstorage`*** keeps the whole collection as one JSON string under `Key`, like `jsonstor-jsonfile`. An origin gets about 5 MB of `localStorage`, shared with everything else it stores; a write past that fails with `QuotaExceededError`.
- ***`jsonstor-browser-opfs`*** keeps the whole collection as one file at `Path` in the Origin Private File System, which allows far more space - gigabytes rather than megabytes.
- ***`jsonstor-browser-indexeddb`*** stores one record per document, so a write changes only that document. IndexedDB keeps a unique index of identifiers, so a search naming one identifier reads that document directly, `StorageInfo()` reports `IndexHostedBy: 'database'`, and `RefreshIndex()` returns `0`.
- ***There is no query language.*** Apart from a lookup by identifier (in IndexedDB, or in a blob storage with `HostIndex: true`), a read loads the whole collection and `jsongin` checks each document.
- ***Documents round-trip through JSON*** in all three, as in every other adapter: a `Date` comes back as a string, and a field set to `undefined` is removed.
- ***All tabs of an origin share one store.*** The two blob storages keep the collection in memory, so if another tab writes the same `Key` or `Path`, call `RefreshIndex()` to re-read it.
- `StorageInfo()` reports the version of `jsongin`, because a browser storage has no version of its own.

Storage Interface
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Every adapter implements the same functions, and they are documented once:
  [Storage Interface](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com/#/guides/Storage-Interface.md).

***The operator list is not repeated here.*** A criteria, a projection, and an update are
  the engine's, and the list changes whenever the engine gains an operator - a copy in this
  file could only ever be out of date. See the
  [Operator Reference](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin/blob/main/docs/guides/Operator-Reference.md).

- [`@liquicode/jsongin`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin) : The query engine.
